meta.parties: Sivagurunathan Et Al. v. Visaladchi Et Al

rules.statement: A person whose title to a share in common property is limited by rights of occupation enjoyed to their exclusion by someone else, lacks the qualification for demanding the exclusion of strangers from the enjoyment (by purchase) of co-proprietary rights under the Thesawalamai.
rules.supporting_quote: "From a practical point of view, a member of a co-parcenary unit of cultivators would always know who precisely were the 'partners' in the enterprise whereby they collectively enjoyed the profits of the common property by their joint exertions. But, particularly in former times when no modern system of registration of titles was in force, persons subject to the Thesawalamai would have found it virtually impossible to trace the identity of strangers claiming interests in the common property (short of full co-proprietorship) who had not previously been admitted into the group of co-sharers. Indeed, I doubt if transactions whereby a man who purchased a share in land subject to a life-interest in favour of someone else were ever contemplated at a time when these customary laws were first introduced into the province of Jaffna."
